newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - January 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - January 24.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Friday's Daily Variety:

* Overseas sales from licensing deals in all media for independently financed films surged to $1.655 billion in fiscal 1996, according to a survey of American Film Marketing Association members by the accounting firm KPMG Peat Markwick. The boost was fueled by the expanding overseas TV market and represents a 21 percent gain in total revenues over last year.

* The "English Patient," followed by "Jerry Maguire," led the list of nominees for the Screen Actors Guild Awards. In television, "Seinfeld" on General Electric's NBC and NYPD Blue on Walt Disney Co's ABC topped the nominations, with four apiece.
* Oliver Stone plans to direct a project that delves into the world of football and would combine the script of "Playing Hurt" at Time Warner Inc's Warner Bros.
* Paramount has acquired screenwriter Joe Eszterhas' new script, "Male Pattern Baldness," for $2 million against $4.5 million, sources said.

* Neil LaBute's dramatic competition film "In the Company of Men," Julie Davis' "I Love You... Don't Touch Me" and Stephen Kay's "The Last Time I Committed Suicide" all made crucial steps toward theatrical release at the 1997 Sundance Film Festival.
* ABC may put "Ellen" in the Tuesday 8:30 spot currently held by the comedy "Life's Work," effective March 4. "Ellen" now appears Wednesday's at 9:30 p.m. EDT.
